argument_macro_structure.dominant_argument_form: Dialectical analysis with cumulative objections and responses, culminating in a dual-sense thesis
argument_macro_structure.premise_explicitness: Moderate – premises often embedded in dialectical exchanges, but key criteria (mind-independence, spatiotemporal vs. abstract location) are explicitly stated

argumentative_quality.dialectical_reasonableness: High – engages with multiple objections (van Inwagen, mind-independence, transitivity, relativity) and offers nuanced replies
argumentative_quality.logical_relevance: High – all objections and replies directly target the central thesis of dual existence senses
argumentative_quality.premise_acceptability: Moderate – relies on contested notions (mind-independence, conceptual spaces) but defends them with examples and analogies

distinctions_drawn: Primary vs. secondary sense of existence
Spatiotemporal location vs. location in abstract space
explicit_definitions_given: Mind-independence as degree to which properties are fixed beyond human control
Concrete entities as those with spatiotemporal location (or at least temporal location)
Abstract entities as those with location in a conceptual/relational space

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: Systematic – addresses objections from transitivity, mind-independence of minds, relativity, van Inwagen's number and quantifier arguments, and Yablo/Gallois metaphor
objections_raised: Existence as a matter of degree (from mind-independence degrees)
Minds/thoughts/people would not exist if mind-independence required
Forces a specific view of time (growing-block)
Van Inwagen: existence tied to univocal number
Van Inwagen: existential quantifier has same truth conditions
Yablo/Gallois: metaphorical existence claims are intractable

epistemic_stance_and_voice.certainty_language_frequency: Moderate – uses hedges like 'seems', 'likely', 'suggests', but also assertive conclusions

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: Conceptual analysis, thought experiments, linguistic observations, appeals to scientific theories (Special Relativity), and historical philosophical positions
named_thought_experiments: Three apples plus three opinions (mixed counting)

philosophical_orientation.grounding: Analytic metaphysics, ontology, philosophy of language
philosophical_orientation.sentiment: Neutral analytic, critical of both univocal and simple pluralist views, defends a nuanced dual-sense view
philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: Existence, mind-independence, abstract vs. concrete entities, ontological commitment, frameworks

structural_organization.structure_type: Sectioned essay with numbered sections (I–VII) and subsections (e.g., III, IV, V, VI), including a Works Cited list

summary_of_core_decisions: The text argues that existence has two distinct senses: a primary, literal sense for concrete entities grounded in spatiotemporal location, and a secondary, metaphorical sense for abstract entities grounded in location in conceptual spaces. It defends this dual-sense view against objections from mind-independence, transitivity, relativity, and van Inwagen's arguments from number and the existential quantifier, concluding that the two senses are irreducible and that the concrete sense is primary.

thesis_commitment.conclusion_type: Qualified pluralism – two senses of existence, not a single univocal sense nor an unrestricted pluralism
thesis_commitment.hedging_density_in_final_paragraph: Low – final section states conclusions confidently, though earlier sections use hedges
